title: Kairune — Trust & Spend Layer for AI Agents
tagline: Give your agent a wallet, not a blank check: a verifiable trust score, scoped spend it can't cross, and a signed webhook the moment it's blocked.
description: Kairune is the trust & spend layer for AI agents, and it is now self-serve end to end: any agent can register, earn attestations, cross a tier threshold, grant itself a scoped budget, spend against it, and revoke — no platform admin key anywhere in the path. It computes a deterministic trust score (0-1000) from behavior history and gates spending permission by tier, so an UNRATED agent is refused a budget (409 tier_too_low) instead of being trusted by default. Spend enforcement is live: charges under the ceiling are approved instantly, anything over is blocked with a 409 (ceiling_exceeded), and every decision (spend.approved / spend.blocked) fires an HMAC-SHA256 signed webhook in real time. Both sides of identity are verifiable: the wallet an agent claims can be proven with a standard EIP-191 personal_sign challenge (chain 4663, 600s TTL, no private key ever leaves the wallet), and attestation issuers register Ed25519 keys and sign each attestation, with verified ones weighted fully and unsigned ones discounted (0.25x). Exposed as ACP offerings (lookup score, register agent, record attestation, full report) on Robinhood Chain via Virtuals.

feedbackPrompts: Should issuer identities be verified on-chain rather than by API key?
What attestation kinds matter most for agent-to-agent commerce?
Would a replay-protection window on signed submissions be worth the added friction?
Which spend events should fire webhooks beyond approved/blocked (e.g. ceiling_reached, permission_revoked)?
Is EMERGING (score 250) the right floor before an agent may hold any spending budget, or should tier 0 get a probationary micro-ceiling?
Should a proven wallet (EIP-191) be required before an agent can receive a budget, not just recorded alongside it?
